item.title: All I-10 lanes closed between Avalon and SR 87 due to downed power line
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Interstate 10 is completely shut down in both directions between Exit 22 at Avalon Boulevard and Exit 31 at State Road 87 following a downed power transmission line near Garcon Point Road in Bagdad, according to Santa Rosa County Communications. The closure went into effect Wednesday afternoon at 2:30 p.m. The duration of the shutdown remains…
item.content:encoded:
Interstate 10 is completely shut down in both directions between Exit 22 at Avalon Boulevard and Exit 31 at State Road 87 following a downed power transmission line near Garcon Point Road in Bagdad, according to Santa Rosa County Communications.

The closure went into effect Wednesday afternoon at 2:30 p.m. The duration of the shutdown remains unknown as utility crews work to address the downed lines. All lanes are affected in both directions.

Traffic is being diverted onto U.S. Highway 90 between Avalon Boulevard and State Road 87, where motorists should prepare for significant delays and increased congestion. Santa Rosa County urges drivers to use extra caution, allow additional travel time, and watch for emergency responders and utility crews in the area.

For real-time traffic updates, check the Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles incident map at trafficincidents.flhsmv.gov or dial 511 on your phone.

item.title: Sen. Scott to speak at HHS Alzheimer's summit in Fort Lauderdale Thursday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott, who chairs the Senate Special Committee on Aging, will deliver remarks Thursday at the Department of Health and Human Services' first-ever Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Summit in Fort Lauderdale. HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. will be a featured speaker at the event, which starts at 1 p.m. and will be…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott, who chairs the Senate Special Committee on Aging, will deliver remarks Thursday at the Department of Health and Human Services' first-ever Alzheimer's Disease and Related Dementias Summit in Fort Lauderdale.

HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. will be a featured speaker at the event, which starts at 1 p.m. and will be followed by a quarterly meeting of the Advisory Council on Alzheimer's Research, Care, and Services. Scott, a Florida Republican, will highlight the importance of advancing Alzheimer's research, improving diagnosis and treatment, and supporting patients, families and caregivers affected by the disease.

Other speakers and participants include Dr. Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services; Kyle Diamantas, acting FDA commissioner; and Michelle Branham, Florida's Secretary of Elder Affairs. Council members representing healthcare systems, neurology, veterans affairs, and Alzheimer's advocacy groups across Florida will also participate.

item.title: Pensacola Doctor Pleads Guilty to Illegal Pill Prescriptions
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A Pensacola physician has admitted to unlawfully distributing thousands of controlled substances in what authorities say was a significant breach of medical ethics and law. Dr. Edward Schott Morrison pleaded guilty to 19 counts of illegally dispensing opioids and stimulant pills. The guilty plea comes as part of an ongoing federal investigation…
item.content:encoded:
A Pensacola physician has admitted to unlawfully distributing thousands of controlled substances in what authorities say was a significant breach of medical ethics and law.

Dr. Edward Schott Morrison pleaded guilty to 19 counts of illegally dispensing opioids and stimulant pills. The guilty plea comes as part of an ongoing federal investigation into prescription drug abuse and doctor-shopping schemes that have fueled addiction crises across the nation.

Morrison is scheduled for sentencing on January 14, 2027. Federal sentencing guidelines for unlawful distribution of controlled substances typically carry substantial prison time, and prosecutors will have the opportunity to present evidence of the scope and impact of Morrison's actions at that hearing.

The case underscores ongoing federal scrutiny of medical providers accused of contributing to the opioid epidemic. The Pensacola area, like much of the Southeast, has grappled with prescription drug abuse and overdose deaths tied in part to overprescribing by healthcare providers.

item.title: Foley police deploy drones as first responders
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Foley Police Department is rolling out a new tool in its public safety arsenal: drones that will respond to emergencies alongside traditional first responders. According to reporting from WPMI NBC 15, the drone program is designed to enhance the department's ability to assess situations quickly and provide real-time information to officers in…
item.content:encoded:
The Foley Police Department is rolling out a new tool in its public safety arsenal: drones that will respond to emergencies alongside traditional first responders.

According to reporting from WPMI NBC 15, the drone program is designed to enhance the department's ability to assess situations quickly and provide real-time information to officers in the field. The move reflects a growing trend among police agencies across the Southeast to adopt unmanned aerial systems for everything from accident scene documentation to search-and-rescue operations.

Details on the specific protocols for drone deployment, training timelines, and which types of calls will trigger a drone response were not immediately available. The Foley Police Department has not yet released additional information about the program's rollout.

item.title: Milton Roofing Company Offers Storm Recovery Resources Thursday
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Action Roofing will replace a homeowner's roof in the Whisper Creek subdivision Thursday morning while offering free educational resources to neighbors navigating storm damage repairs. Following severe weather in the Milton area, homeowners face questions about roof repairs, contractor selection, and insurance claims. Action Roofing will set up a…
item.content:encoded:
Action Roofing will replace a homeowner's roof in the Whisper Creek subdivision Thursday morning while offering free educational resources to neighbors navigating storm damage repairs.

Following severe weather in the Milton area, homeowners face questions about roof repairs, contractor selection, and insurance claims. Action Roofing will set up a community resource tent at 4731 Perception Circle from 7 a.m. to 11 a.m. to distribute materials on choosing qualified contractors, documenting damage, understanding the repair process, and avoiding scams. Company representatives will be available to answer roofing-related questions at no obligation.

Topics covered will include common factors affecting roof repairs, Florida building code requirements, contractor vetting questions, damage documentation, and insurance deductibles. Homeowners with specific insurance questions should contact their insurance company or a licensed insurance professional. The company, founded in 1986, operates in seven Florida cities and has assisted in recovery from dozens of hurricanes.

item.content:encoded: Three major financial institutions are backing relief efforts for Escambia and Santa Rosa County residents affected by Hurricane Isaias. Hancock Whitney has pledged $50,000 to the United Way of West Florida's Recovery Fund, while Navy Federal Credit Union is contributing $100,000. Florida Blue has also made a donation to the fund, though the specific amount was not disclosed. The Recovery Fund is designed to help households in the two counties recover from storm damage.

item.title: Escambia County advances vote on massive Beulah development plan
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Commission unanimously approved moving forward with a controversial development proposal last week, paving the way for a final hearing next month on the sprawling Outlying Fields (OLF-8) project. All five commissioners voted to advance an ordinance that would adopt the master plan and design code for the 540-acre property in…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Commission unanimously approved moving forward with a controversial development proposal last week, paving the way for a final hearing next month on the sprawling Outlying Fields (OLF-8) project.

All five commissioners voted to advance an ordinance that would adopt the master plan and design code for the 540-acre property in Beulah. The move sets up a final hearing scheduled for November 5, when the commission will consider formally approving the framework.

The Outlying Fields project has drawn attention from residents and planning advocates concerned about the scope of development on the county's outskirts. The master plan and design code will guide how the massive parcel is developed over time.

item.title: Historic Pensacola Haunted Tours Return for Halloween Weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: History buffs and ghost hunters can explore Pensacola's spookier side this weekend with the 36th Annual Haunted House Walking Tours, according to InWeekly's arts and events calendar. Historic Pensacola is offering two tour options Friday and Saturday — the Haunted History Walking Tour and the Macabre Museum Walking Tour — each designed to guide…
item.content:encoded:
History buffs and ghost hunters can explore Pensacola's spookier side this weekend with the 36th Annual Haunted House Walking Tours, according to InWeekly's arts and events calendar.

Historic Pensacola is offering two tour options Friday and Saturday — the Haunted History Walking Tour and the Macabre Museum Walking Tour — each designed to guide visitors through the city's reportedly haunted properties while sharing tales of Pensacola's past. Tours depart at 6:30 p.m., 7:30 p.m., and 8:30 p.m. on both October 23 and 24.

Tickets are $15 to $20 per person and can be purchased online at historicpensacola.org. The tours offer a seasonal blend of local history and entertainment ahead of Halloween.

Director Justin Gaylard, who first experienced the iconic film at midnight showings at Silver Screen Theater during his ninth-grade years, is helming the production. The stage adaptation follows the same campy, interactive spirit of the beloved…
item.content:encoded:
The cast of "The Rocky Horror Show" is ready to bring the cult classic to life on stage in Pensacola. Director Justin Gaylard, who first experienced the iconic film at midnight showings at Silver Screen Theater during his ninth-grade years, is helming the production.

The stage adaptation follows the same campy, interactive spirit of the beloved "Rocky Horror Picture Show" that has captivated audiences for decades. Cast members have spent weeks perfecting the choreography and performances, including mastering that famous step to the right.

Gaylard's personal connection to Rocky Horror in Pensacola — those formative midnight screenings at a local theater — now comes full circle as he directs the stage version for audiences in the community where he first fell in love with the show.

The race marks a rematch of sorts, with Myers seeking to return to the council seat she previously held.

item.title: Spectrum Says 99% of Hurricane Outages Restored, But Some Customers Losing Service Again
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Spectrum says service has been restored to approximately 99% of customers affected by Hurricane Isaias, but the continuing cleanup is creating new outages in some Northwest Florida neighborhoods. Spectrum Public Affairs Manager Tracy White says extensive tree and infrastructure damage in the Pensacola area has…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Spectrum says service has been restored to approximately 99% of customers affected by Hurricane Isaias, but the continuing cleanup is creating new outages in some Northwest Florida neighborhoods.

Spectrum Public Affairs Manager Tracy White says extensive tree and infrastructure damage in the Pensacola area has complicated the restoration process.

As trees are removed, utility poles are replaced and heavy equipment moves through neighborhoods, communications lines that Spectrum crews have already repaired are sometimes damaged or have to be moved again.

In some cases, that means customers who had their internet, television or phone service restored are losing it a second time.

Several heavily damaged areas also remain difficult or unsafe for technicians to access.

Spectrum has brought crews into the area from Florida, Texas, the Carolinas, Virginia and Tennessee to assist with restoration.

The company says crews will continue working remaining outages as damaged areas become accessible.

Spectrum previously announced automatic bill credits and free equipment replacement for customers affected by the hurricane.

Customers who lose service again during neighborhood cleanup or see damaged Spectrum lines are encouraged to report the problem directly to the company.

item.title: Millions of Cubic Yards of Hurricane Debris Await Removal Across Northwest Florida
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Hundreds of thousands of cubic yards of Hurricane Isaias debris have already disappeared from Northwest Florida roadsides, but local governments say millions more remain. Escambia County contractors have collected approximately 330,000 cubic yards of storm debris in more than 7,400 loads. That total does not…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Hundreds of thousands of cubic yards of Hurricane Isaias debris have already disappeared from Northwest Florida roadsides, but local governments say millions more remain.

Escambia County contractors have collected approximately 330,000 cubic yards of storm debris in more than 7,400 loads. That total does not include additional debris collected by county employees.

The county estimates Hurricane Isaias generated approximately 2.2 million cubic yards of vegetative debris.

About 236 collection units are currently working throughout Escambia County, along with 40 bucket trucks assisting with damaged and fallen trees.

Across the county line, Santa Rosa County has collected more than 250,000 cubic yards of vegetative debris and more than 200 cubic yards of construction and demolition material.

Santa Rosa recently increased its estimate of total storm debris from 1.5 million to 1.8 million cubic yards. The county estimates removal will cost approximately $23 million.

The City of Pensacola says contractors have collected more than 3,200 loads. The city's contractor projects the Pensacola cleanup will ultimately involve approximately one million cubic yards of debris.

Milton is dealing with an unusually large amount of debris for a city covering only about six square miles.

City Manager Ed Spears told NewsRadio 92.3 that Milton estimates approximately 400,000 cubic yards of vegetative debris and another 35,000 cubic yards of construction and demolition material were generated by the storm.

Milton expects debris removal to continue through the end of November.

All four jurisdictions are planning multiple collection passes.

Residents are being asked to keep vegetative material separate from construction and demolition debris and avoid placing piles where they block roads, drainage systems, fire hydrants or utilities.

item.title: Okaloosa County consolidates disaster aid centers at Rigdon location
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Okaloosa County is consolidating its Multi-Agency Resource Centers (MARCs) at a single new location beginning Monday, October 26 at 1 p.m., according to a press release from the county. The new consolidated MARC will operate at the Destin-Fort Walton Rigdon Center, located at the former NWF Fairgrounds. Two existing locations are closing: the…
item.content:encoded:
Okaloosa County is consolidating its Multi-Agency Resource Centers (MARCs) at a single new location beginning Monday, October 26 at 1 p.m., according to a press release from the county.

The new consolidated MARC will operate at the Destin-Fort Walton Rigdon Center, located at the former NWF Fairgrounds. Two existing locations are closing: the Crestview Community Center closes at the end of business Thursday, October 22, and the Destin-Fort Walton Beach Convention Center closes at the end of business Saturday, October 24.

County officials say residents seeking assistance should bring identification, proof of residence, insurance information, and other documentation related to disaster-related losses to ensure they receive appropriate aid. The resource centers have been helping residents navigate recovery and relief resources following recent disasters in the region.

item.title: FPL Offers Qualifying Hurricane Victims Up to $3,200 in Financial Assistance
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Some Florida Power & Light customers recovering from Hurricane Isaias could qualify for as much as $3,200 in combined assistance for electric bills and repairs to damaged electrical equipment. FPL has expanded assistance through its Saving Steps and Care To Share programs following the hurricane. Saving Steps is…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Some Florida Power & Light customers recovering from Hurricane Isaias could qualify for as much as $3,200 in combined assistance for electric bills and repairs to damaged electrical equipment.

FPL has expanded assistance through its Saving Steps and Care To Share programs following the hurricane.

Saving Steps is providing a $200 bill credit to nearly 10,000 previously income-qualified customers in areas affected by Isaias.

The program uses broader income eligibility than many traditional government assistance programs. Eligibility varies based on household size, income, county and the specific program.

FPL says Care To Share can provide qualifying customers with up to $2,000 for repairs to customer-owned electrical equipment damaged by the storm.

That can include equipment such as meter boxes and weatherheads that must be repaired before a home can safely receive electricity.

Care To Share can also provide up to $1,000 toward qualifying customers' electric bills.

Combined with the Saving Steps credit, assistance could total as much as $3,200 for some households.

FPL says the goal is to help customers with expenses that remain after the utility completes repairs to its own electrical system.

Customers have to meet eligibility requirements and should apply through FPL's assistance programs.

item.title: Escambia School Board Approves Additional Book Removals After Lengthy Public Opposition
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County School Board members unanimously approved another round of book removals Tuesday night, one day after a federal appeals court ruled board members can be required to testify about earlier decisions to remove books from district libraries. The board voted 4-0 to approve Superintendent Keith Leonard's…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, FL (NewsRadio 92.3) -- Escambia County School Board members unanimously approved another round of book removals Tuesday night, one day after a federal appeals court ruled board members can be required to testify about earlier decisions to remove books from district libraries.

The board voted 4-0 to approve Superintendent Keith Leonard's recommendation to remove titles covered by the district's June 2025 directive concerning books appearing on the Florida Department of Education's book-removal list.

The action removes affected titles from district media centers, classroom libraries and recommended-reading lists.

The vote followed lengthy public comment from residents, parents and school media specialists both supporting and opposing the district's book policies.

Opponents cited titles including "Harriet the Spy," "Roll of Thunder, Hear My Cry," "Roots" and "Are You There God? It's Me, Margaret?" while arguing books should be evaluated individually.

One district media specialist told the board that parents already have the ability to limit what their children can check out or prevent their children from accessing school libraries altogether.

Parent Kristen Moschel also argued individual families should decide which books their children read.

Board members did not discuss the removal recommendation among themselves before voting unanimously to approve it.

The meeting came one day after the 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals upheld a lower-court decision requiring School Board members to sit for depositions in an ongoing federal lawsuit over previous book removals.

Board members had argued legislative privilege protected them from being compelled to testify about their decisions.

The appeals court concluded that the specific book-removal votes at issue involved applying existing School Board policies and were administrative rather than legislative acts.

The ruling does not decide the underlying lawsuit over whether the district's book removals violated the First Amendment.

item.title: Highway 182 resurfacing project starts Monday in Santa Rosa County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Drivers heading through Santa Rosa County should plan for delays starting next week. Beginning Monday, October 26, work crews will begin a major resurfacing and widening project on Highway 182 between Chumuckla Highway and Allison Creek Lane, according to Santa Rosa County Communications. The project is expected to run through October 2027,…
item.content:encoded:
Drivers heading through Santa Rosa County should plan for delays starting next week. Beginning Monday, October 26, work crews will begin a major resurfacing and widening project on Highway 182 between Chumuckla Highway and Allison Creek Lane, according to Santa Rosa County Communications.

The project is expected to run through October 2027, weather permitting. Work will take place between 7 a.m. and 5 p.m. weekdays, and Highway 182 will be reduced to a single lane during paving operations. Santa Rosa County officials warn motorists to expect heavy delays, use caution in the work zone, and follow directions from flaggers and posted traffic control signs.

The improvements will include milling and resurfacing the roadway, replacing and upgrading culverts, re-establishing ditches, widening shoulders with rumble strips, adding pavement striping, and installing raised reflective pavement markers. More details and maps of the project area are available on the Santa Rosa County website.

item.title: Baldwin County Sees Spike in Bat Bites; Thomas Hospital Treats Six
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Thomas Hospital in Baldwin County, Alabama, has treated six patients for bat bites as the region experiences a rise in incidents, according to WKRG-TV 5. The uptick in bat-related injuries has raised concerns about potential rabies exposure, a serious public health risk. Health officials typically recommend immediate medical attention and…
item.content:encoded:
Thomas Hospital in Baldwin County, Alabama, has treated six patients for bat bites as the region experiences a rise in incidents, according to WKRG-TV 5.

The uptick in bat-related injuries has raised concerns about potential rabies exposure, a serious public health risk. Health officials typically recommend immediate medical attention and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) vaccination for anyone bitten by a bat, since rabies is nearly always fatal once symptoms appear.

Bat bites can occur when the animals enter homes or come into contact with people outdoors. Experts advise residents to avoid handling bats directly and to seek medical care promptly if exposure occurs. Anyone who suspects contact with a bat should contact local health authorities or visit an emergency room.
